newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro Disney H1 loss widens as charges rise.
newsitem.headline: Euro Disney H1 loss widens as charges rise.

text.p: Euro Disney, the operator of the Disneyland Paris theme park, reported on Tuesday that its loss for the first half of the 1996/97 year widened as debt charges rose faster than operating income.
The company showed a net loss for the six months to March 31, its traditional low season, of 210 million francs ($36 million), compared with a loss of 169 million for the first half of 1995/96.
The deterioration in its results, the first year-over-year downturn in more than two years of improvement, was due to a 68 million franc jump in lease and financial expenses to 356 million.

The surge in charges had been anticipated as Euro Disney took on payments that had been temporarily suspended by a 1994 debt restructuring accord to keep the fledgling company from collapsing under a huge debt burden.
As part of the repayment schedule, its expenses began to climb last year but the biggest increase -- around 200 million francs -- was pencilled in for the 1996/97 fiscal year.

Euro Disney's first-half income before lease and financial charges jumped to 120 million francs from 58 million, helped by a 12.5 percent rise in attendance, higher hotel occupancy rates and higher spending-per-visitor. Lower interest rates also contributed to offsetting part of the rise in expenses.

A spokesman for Euro Disney said the company was pleased with the results given the weak spending climate in Europe and the increase in its expenses. "Offsetting this big increase wasn't easy," he said. "This is the most challenging year."
The company said in its earnings statement that the decision to hold 1997 prices at 1996 levels was boosting attendance but "limiting the company's potential to improve its margins this year".
The commercial appeal of Euro Disney, 39 percent owned by The Walt Disney Co, is no longer in doubt. It recently celebrated its fifth anniversary as the most popular tourist attraction in Europe.
"The fifth anniversary promotional momentum is now under way," chairman Gilles Pelisson was quoted as saying in the statement.

"The success of Disneyland Paris is growing as is our ability to manage the seasonal fluctuations in the business. However, growth in the high season remains vital to counter the sharp increases in financial charges," Pelisson said. ($ = 5.832 French Francs)
